issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-5a0dc962. This child removes the blocker that made the parent unachievable.

build.rs embeds `date -u` output at build time, so two builds of byte-identical source always hash differently. pinned-binaries/bead-pre-feature.metadata.json records "sha256 is NOT reproducible across rebuilds: build.rs re-embeds BEAD_BUILD_TIMESTAMP... never [verify] by rebuilding." That makes the parent's acceptance ("running the script for the pinned SHA reproduces the recorded sha256") unsatisfiable as written, and is the likely root cause of 22 failures.

Fix: when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set, derive the embedded BEAD_BUILD_TIMESTAMP from it (UTC, same %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ format) instead of invoking `date`; when unset, keep current behavior exactly. scripts/build-from-archive.sh (child beadrs chain) then sets SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to the committer date of <sha>, so a given commit always builds to identical bytes.

Acceptance:
- With SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixed, two builds of the same extracted tree produce identical sha256 (use separate CARGO_TARGET_DIRs or a clean between builds so cargo caching cannot mask it). If absolute scratch paths leak into the binary, neutralize with --remap-path-prefix and note it.
- Without SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, `bead --version` still carries a fresh build timestamp; existing tests pass unchanged.
- The embedded commit stays "unknown" for git-archive trees (no .git dir). Do not try to re-embed a commit into archive builds; the sha lives in the metadata file.
- cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test all clean.
issue.title: Make builds hash-reproducible by honoring SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH in build.rs

Add CLI regression coverage for divergent/remote-advanced/equal-sequence/behind conflicts, suppression flags, and concurrent healthy claims. Preserve all histories; no automatic restore, reorigin, or Git mutation. Acceptance: targeted safety tests plus cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test pass. Scope: src/main.rs, src/service/reconcile.rs, relevant native store/publication integration and new isolated tests/spec.

issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-8c343a7c (claim-epoch fencing umbrella). Child 3 of 5 - the single sanctioned recovery path around child 2's fence.

Problem:
Once the credential is mandatory, legitimate operator recovery (a dead worker still holding a live-looking claim) needs a way through. That path must be explicit and loud, and omission must never silently mean override.

Scope:
- Add one explicit reason-bearing override to the fenced claimant-owned mutations (or a dedicated recovery command) that permits the mutation without the current credential.
- Omitting the credential without the override conflicts; passing the override without a reason is a usage error. Do not let omission mean override.
- Emit a distinct, machine-readable audit/change-feed event kind for every override, recording actor, reason, target issue, and the epoch that was overridden.
- Overrides stay inside the same IMMEDIATE transaction as the mutation they permit, including audit, resource locks, attempt receipts, and checkpoint publication.
- Document that overrides are for operator recovery, never for automation.

Acceptance:
- A claimed mutation with override plus reason succeeds and records the distinct override event in the audit trail and the change feed.
- An override without a reason fails as a usage error and changes nothing.
- An automated consumer supplying neither credential nor override still conflicts with exit code 4.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Add explicit reason-bearing operator override with a distinct audit event

issue.description:
AGENTS.md declares that NEEDLE compatibility is defined by research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md and that compatibility must never be claimed without passing the corresponding conformance suite, but the only NEEDLE coverage in tracked work is per-feature canaries at individual release gates (redaction remediation, claim-epoch consumer canary). There is no bead maintaining a contract-level suite, so a CLI change can quietly break a behavioral fact of the contract that no current feature's canary exercises. Inventory the behavioral facts in the spec, map each to an automated conformance test (adding the missing ones), and wire the suite into the release gate so NEEDLE-compatibility regressions fail before release rather than at canary time.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Give the NEEDLE compatibility contract a standing conformance suite (needle-cli-contract-v1)

issue.description:
ADR-004 makes the pinned `cargo +1.85 check --all-targets` lane the only thing keeping the declared MSRV honest ('honest today by luck, not by verification') and requires that 'the lane must pin the same version the manifest declares; drift between them is a CI failure, not a doc nit.' No open bead tracks that parity requirement. Add an assertion — script or CI step — that fails the run when the bead-rs-ci WorkflowTemplate's pinned toolchain differs from rust-version in Cargo.toml, and verify the lane actually runs check --all-targets (not just check). The lane lives in the Argo Workflows template in declarative-config per the org CI rules (no GitHub Actions).

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Assert the bead-rs-ci pinned MSRV lane toolchain matches the manifest's rust-version
